page: Microsoft Azure D8lds_v5 is a virtual machine instance built on the DLDSv5 family, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 virtual CPUs, which map to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory allocation stands at 16.0 GB, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. Local storage is provided via a bundled 307 GB SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark evaluations place the D8lds_v5 consistently in the average performance tier across most workloads. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a single-core stress-ng score of 1897.88 and a multi-core score of 7760.65. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported by hardware-level flags including AVX-512 and AES, reflected in a Passmark CPU encryption score of 7320.19. Memory performance shows a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 419.63 GB/sec, while large block uncached read and write speeds reach 58.77 GB/sec and 41.56 GB/sec respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 31.24 GB/sec, whereas single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average rate of 28.45 GB/sec.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the D8lds_v5 represents a compute-oriented configuration designed for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but have modest memory footprints. This resource density makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for tasks where high memory overhead is unnecessary, avoiding the premium associated with memory-optimized instances. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 11.32 GB/sec, lightweight database operations, Redis key-value stores processing up to 7.97 million SET operations per second, and small-scale machine learning tasks like 135M parameter LLM inference.

Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance offers a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a compute-focused option for memory-lean workloads. Benchmark data indicates average tier performance across most metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1595.0 and multi-core score of 6034.0. It supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES for cryptographic and vector acceleration.
